scope: Five matched original timed Mars cases plus targeted +0.90 ablations; offline analysis only.

physics_launch_source.post_launch_difference: Live offroad_control.py subsequently received a module-docstring clarification and a held-request diagnostic alignment correction (multiplying recorded requested velocity by travel priority). Controller commands and completed physics results were not changed; launch-code claims refer to this archived source, not live bytes.

execution_and_output_counts.interpretation: The five V2 cases were separately launched and executed. Matching payloads identify identical saved output, not copied/reused evidence and not statistically varied independent trials.

destination_sample_metric_definitions.nominal_timed_reference_within_50mm_samp: All saved samples within 50 mm of their original time-indexed reference.
destination_sample_metric_definitions.nominal_final_goal_last_second_within_50: Samples during the final one second within 50 mm of the fixed nominal final goal.
destination_sample_metric_definitions.caveat: These fractions describe samples, not completion progress along a closed or self-intersecting route. They do not establish settling or attitude safety.

interpretation: The prototype lowers original-path moving RMS in four of five initial cases but markedly regresses +0.90 figure-eight tracking and attitude. It is not promoted.
Capping/projecting a feedback reference can make managed tracking error small while the robot remains far from the original timed path. Both errors and their reference gap are reported.

Accepted-reference residual is the logged load-weighted RMS of individual estimated-contact planar kinematic residuals after the common accepted body velocity. It is distinct from mismatch against measured body motion and is not proof of no slip.
The initial five-case baseline belongs to this campaign; earlier D10 and W20 baselines must not be substituted for it.
Targeted catch-up/position-cap ablations test only +0.90 and cannot establish improvement across all five cases or identify a unique cause by themselves.

V2 changes the position-error cap from 0.05 m to 1 m and retains catch-up gain 1/s; the modal allocator math is unchanged. It is evaluated as a separate five-case family, preserving the initial prototype and all ablations.

Fixed-contact regression establishes finite bounded allocation and an accepted horizontal body reference consistent with that allocation. It does not establish robot-level balance, nominal-destination recovery, friction feasibility, or robust behavior through changing contacts.

The final balance-guard family retains the 1 m position cap and catch-up gain 1/s, scaling travel requests, catch-up, projected position error, and nominal acceleration with a default-off smooth guard. It does not change the nominal trajectory clock, gain library, or holding torques; reduced travel demand does not guarantee autonomous progress.
Completion means the requested duration ran without a fall. Nominal destination accuracy, balance, saturation, and settling remain separate criteria.
